scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 10 (TUH, 7nm vs 14nm) with Table I/II/IV setup; Figure 9 MLTD for gobmk
scenario.description: HotGauge case study of a 7-core Skylake-like client CPU in 14/10/7nm. Single-threaded SPEC2006 workloads were run on each core after idle warmup. Time until hotspot (Tth=80C, MLTD_th=25C, radius 1 mm) was measured with 3D-ICE transient simulation. Per-block x, y, width, height and power values are not published in the paper text; only core area (5, 2.5, 1.25 mm2), a 3x2 core aspect ratio, ~5 mm2 die, a 5 GHz/1.4 V operating point and power density >8 W/mm2 for bzip2 are given.
scenario.architecture: 7-core out-of-order Skylake-like client CPU, SMT2, 224-entry ROB, private L1/L2, shared 16 MiB ring L3, at 14/10/7nm
scenario.workload: Single-threaded SPEC2006 benchmarks (e.g. gcc, gobmk, bzip2, milc), run per core, 200M-instruction region of interest, 1M-cycle time steps
scenario.operating_point: 5 GHz, 1.4 V (turbo); 40C local ambient; idle warmup or cold start; HS483-ND heatsink with P14752-ND fan at 6000 rpm

original_setup.solver: 3D-ICE v3.0.0 compact transient thermal model (CTTM), run in a perf-power-therm co-simulation chain with Sniper (instruction-window-centric/ROB model) and a modified McPAT v1.2. Thermal grid resolution is 100 um (PDF pp. 2-4).
original_setup.optimizer: None. HotGauge is a characterization methodology, not an optimizer. The mitigation case studies (PDF pp. 9-10) manually scale unit or IC area and do not run an automated optimization.
original_setup.controller: None. No closed-loop thermal controller or DVFS/throttling is simulated. Fixed power traces are fed to the thermal model, and throttling is only discussed as a consequence.
original_setup.benchmark: HotGauge case study of a 7-core Skylake-like client CPU at 14/10/7 nm, 5 GHz and 1.4 V. SPEC2006 single-threaded workloads (e.g. gcc, gobmk, bzip2, milc) run on each core individually after a cold start or idle warmup. 200M-instruction region of interest, 1M-cycle time steps. Scenario figures: Fig. 10 (TUH) and Fig. 9 (MLTD), with the setup in Tables I, II and IV (PDF pp. 3-8).

thermal_observable.location: Time until the first hotspot (T > 80 C and MLTD > 25 C within a 1 mm radius) anywhere on the die in the 7nm processor, for a single-threaded SPEC2006 workload run on a core
thermal_observable.aggregation: 5th percentile of TUH across SPEC2006 benchmarks (each run on each core) after idle warmup, 7nm. The 25th and 50th percentiles are 0.4 ms and 0.6 ms. The 14nm values are 0.4, 0.6 and 1.2 ms. Source: Fig. 10 caption.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper observable is a transient time-until-hotspot (TUH, a hotspot-detection time) from a time-resolved 3D-ICE simulation. A steady-state or single-row-power-trace 2D run cannot reproduce it.

The thermal stack is a layered vertical model: active layer plus bulk silicon, solder TIM, copper heat spreader, thermal grease and a HS483-ND heatsink with a P14752-ND fan at 6000 rpm. A simple 2D die model does not capture this vertical heat path or the cooling.
The solver is 3D-ICE v3.0.0 with non-uniform initial temperature (idle or cold warmup). The cooling and package model differ from any Studio solver.

Power comes from Sniper+McPAT time-varying per-unit traces (1M-cycle steps, many units per core, plus AVX512, System Agent, IMC and I/O additions). The paper publishes no per-block power values or trace, and a one-row power trace would not reproduce workload-dependent hotspots.
The hotspot metrics (MLTD within a 1 mm radius, severity sigmoid) are not temperature-only observables. The runner's temperatures cannot be compared numerically to the paper's TUH.
There is no optimizer or controller in the original setup, and no reliability model beyond the threshold-based severity metric. These do not map onto optimizer-based or controller-based Studio flows.

Interposer, 3D stacking and chiplets are not modeled. The setup is a single monolithic 2D die (about 5 mm2 core area at 14nm), with 7 cores, node-scaled area (5/2.5/1.25 mm2 per core) and a 3x2 core aspect ratio.

studio_assumptions: No Studio package or material assumptions are provided in the packet, so none are asserted.

Any Studio placement built from dimensions and powers would be a separate illustrative 2D construction. Its generated coordinates are not paper-derived facts and must not be compared numerically with the paper's TUH.
No exact replication of the paper's results is claimed.

methods.note: Text-level method claims match the paper: 3D-ICE v3.0.0, Sniper ROB model, modified McPAT v1.2, Definition 1 on p5 (Tth 80C, MLTD 25C, radius 1mm), TUH definition on p8, and the absence of a controller or optimizer. The extraction correctly says the TUH observable is transient and not reproducible by a steady 2D run. The Fig. 6 algorithm and Figs. 9-11 are only in extracted text, with no visual verification. The no-controller and no-interposer claims are inferred from absence, not stated.

code.note: No assets are pinned. The GitHub repo and Zenodo DOIs 5523504 and 5523535 are bare links on p1 and p13, so they were not inspected and prove nothing about scripts, inputs or versions.

parameters.note: Table I and p3 text values were reconfirmed: core areas 5/2.5/1.25 mm2, 7 cores, 5 GHz, 1.4 V, 100 um grid, 1M-cycle step, 200M-instruction ROI, Table II and IV values, and unit conversions all correct. However the paper has an unflagged internal contradiction on L3 (Table I says 16 MiB, p3 text says 512 KiB 4-way), and an ambiguity between a ~5 mm2 die and a 5 mm2 per-core area at 14nm. The extraction repeats these inconsistently. Core-orientation of the 3x2 aspect ratio is unspecified.

assessment.summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped; simulation_allowed=false). The gate failed because the custom experiment has no blocks and no power_w object (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false), so the final verdict is blocked and comparison_valid=false. The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so even if it had run it would produce only a steady-state result with no transient trace. The paper's observable is a transient time-until-hotspot (TUH) of 0.2 ms (5th percentile, 7nm, idle warmup; 25th/50th percentiles 0.4/0.6 ms, and 14nm 0.4/0.6/1.2 ms). It comes from a 3D-ICE v3.0.0 transient co-simulation with Sniper and McPAT, a layered vertical stack with heatsink and fan, and hotspot criteria of T>80 C and MLTD>25 C within 1 mm. No Studio output exists, so no numerical comparison is made. Any 2D steady temperature would differ in location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions, so only qualitative sensitivity could be discussed, such as smaller 7nm cores and higher power density shortening TUH. This is not an exact replication and no replication is claimed. This is not a bundled EV6/GCC adapted demonstration, and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace sizes and powers were provided. No illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was generated, so there is no source commit or placement assumption to report. The linked HotGauge GitHub repository and Zenodo archives (DOIs 5523504 and 5523535) were not pinned or inspected, and their contents are unverified. Only Table I areas (5, 2.5 and 1.25 mm2 per core), the 3:2 core aspect ratio, the 5 GHz/1.4 V operating point and the bzip2 power density lower bound (>8 W/mm2) are available. These cannot be turned into per-block coordinates or watts without an unpublished rule.
limitations: Studio was skipped; there is no simulation output, so no temperature, TUH or MLTD comparison is possible.

The gate failed: the custom experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w object. The floorplan block coordinates and per-block powers are not published numerically (Fig. 5 is image-only and no Sniper/McPAT power values are given).

Essential physical mismatches: the paper's TUH is a transient hotspot-detection time (3D-ICE, idle/cold warmup, 1M-cycle steps), whereas the experiment is a steady-state custom 2D run with no transient trace.

Mismatches in boundary assumptions: the paper uses a layered vertical stack (active and bulk silicon, solder TIM, copper spreader, thermal grease, HS483-ND heatsink with P14752-ND fan at 6000 rpm) and a 40 C local ambient; no Studio package or material assumptions are provided to match this.

Mismatches in aggregation and location: the paper reports a 5th-percentile TUH across SPEC2006 benchmarks and cores, anywhere on the die, using hotspot criteria (T>80 C and MLTD>25 C within 1 mm) that are not temperature-only observables.
The paper's time-varying per-unit workload power traces cannot be reproduced by any single-row power input.
